events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a driver-initiated no-show cancellation, so NS-0 routes the $6.61 fee to the NS-1/NS-2 test [F3][RD-2 not applicable][NS-0]. The trace settles the three limbs: (i) pass (a tap at 12:05:55) [F5], (ii) fail — 601 m at the tap, closest approach 545 m overall, never inside 200 m [F5][F1], (iii) fail — 0 s inside the radius after the tap [F5][F2]. Under NS-1 all of (i)(ii)(iii) must hold, so the fee cannot stand [F1][F3][NS-1].

The driver's statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] and the 12:06 chat "I'm here already" [F9] are contradicted by the GPS/timeline records: he stood stationary 3 min 30 s at 600 m from the pickup, not at it [F2][F5], and system records override statements [F1][F9][NS-1]. Duration alone (3 min 30 s) does not cure a wait served outside the pickup location [F2][F3][NS-1].

Accordingly NS-2 applies: the fee of $6.61, recorded on the fare [F7] for an unconsummated RydeX booking with no surge [F8], is refunded in full to the rider [F3][F7][NS-2]. Refund is issued as a Ryde voucher, no cash [F7][NS-7].

Independently, NS-2's account-review condition is met: a recorded "I'm Here" tap [F5] while GPS placed the driver 601 m outside the pickup range [F1] is the fake-arrival-tap trigger. The driver's otherwise clean record (0 disputes upheld in 502 trips) [F17] is a profile fact and cannot defeat the trigger [F5][F1][NS-2].

Amount = cancellation fee $6.61 as recorded on the fare [F3][F7][NS-2]. No separate detour or FARE arithmetic applies (no off-route segment facts in this file) [F3][NS-0].

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee was charged as a rider no-show, so its validity must be tested against NS-1: the driver had to press "I'm Here", be within the pickup range when doing so, and wait there over 3 minutes.
NS-1(i) fails on the platform's own records: the timeline shows the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so a no-show fee cannot stand.

NS-1(ii) fails: GPS shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 545 m and he never entered the 200 m arrival radius at any time, so he was never "at the pick-up location according to GPS data".

The driver's claimed 3+ minute wait did not occur at the pickup point: he was stationary for 3 min 30 s at coordinates 600 m away, and his in-range waiting time after the supposed arrival was 0 seconds.

The driver's written claim that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the system records (no button press, never within 200 m), and the driver's chat message at 12:05:55 asserted "I'm here already" while he was 601 m from the pickup point — system records win over statements.

Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) each fail, NS-2 requires the full $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded to the rider, and the rider's own conduct is consistent with waiting at the pickup point (0 prior disputes, 4.7 rating).

The driver pressed nothing per the timeline yet falsely signalled arrival in chat while 601 m away and cancelled — conduct matching Ryde's listed abuse of the arrival/cancellation button, so a flag_account referral on the driver is warranted.

weaknesses: The timeline contains an internal inconsistency the other side will use: F5 says the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:05:55 while 601 m away, but F6 says driver_pressed_here_at is null — the driver will cite F5 to argue a press occurred. Even on F5's version he was 601 m outside the pickup range with 0 s inside it, so NS-1(ii)/(iii) still fail.

The driver's chat messages (F9, F11) and statement (F12) purport to show a real 3+ minute wait, and the rider's reply (F10) does not prove the rider's own location — the rider has no GPS proof of being at the pickup.
The rider's 90-day record is clean (F16) but equally the driver has 0 prior disputes in 90 days over 502 trips (F17), which the driver will use to resist any account flag.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here" (at 12:05:55) and then waited 3 min 30 s without cancelling, satisfying the waiting-duration limb of the no-show rule; the rider's claim that he was "never there" must be tested limb by limb and not treated as automatic.

The platform's own timeline is internally inconsistent with any genuine arrival: one field records the "I'm Here" tap at 12:05:55 and another records no tap at all, so the record of arrival cannot be relied on as proof the conditions were met.

The driver's own statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by GPS: he tapped 601 m from the pickup point and was never within 200 m of it at any time.

The vehicle's closest approach to the pickup was 545 m at 12:05:20 and it then stood still 600 m away from 12:05:35 until the 12:09:05 cancellation, so the driver was not at the pickup point during the alleged wait.

The 200 m proximity condition was never met: cumulative time inside 200 m was 0 seconds, and the driver never entered that range after the tap, so condition (ii) of the no-show rule fails for the entire waiting period.

The driver's chat message "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out" at 12:06 was false as to location, since he was roughly 600 m away at that moment; the rider's reply confirms he was at the pickup point and saw no car.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is recorded on the fare and was charged to the rider although the driver-initiated no-show did not satisfy the required conditions, so the fee must be returned in full.

Because the timeline shows an "I'm Here" tap while GPS shows the driver outside the pickup-point range at that moment, the account-review condition for misuse of the arrival button is triggered alongside the refund, independently of the merits of the underlying wait.

weaknesses: The driver did in fact tap "I'm Here" and then stayed stationary for 3 min 30 s, which on its face looks like compliance with the wait requirement (F5, F2, F3) — the rider's side will argue the substance of NS-1 was met and only the radius was missed.
Timeline fact F5 (a tap recorded) conflicts with F6 (no tap on record), so the driver can argue the arrival record is unreliable rather than clearly false (F5, F6).
The driver has a clean history — 502 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F17) — which supports a no-penalty treatment and undercuts any escalation beyond the refund.
The rider's own status is strong (3.7-year account, rating 4.7, 0 disputes, F16), but profile facts cannot decide the case; my case rests on the GPS record (F1, F2, F5).

points.response: Agreed limb by limb — and limb (i) and (ii) both fail, not just the radius: the timeline records no "I'm Here" tap (F6) and GPS puts the driver 601 m away at the moment of the alleged tap (F5, F1). The 3 min 30 s stationary period in F2 was spent 600 m from the pickup, so it is not a wait "at the pick-up location" under NS-1 and the fee is not saved by duration alone.

This point is conceded on the record's reliability, but it does not help the driver: under NS-1 the condition to be proved is that the driver WAS at the pickup point according to GPS, and the GPS limb fails on every reading (F5, F1, F2) — an unreliable button record cannot manufacture compliance with NS-1(ii).

No disagreement — the driver's statement in F12 that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by GPS (F1, F5) and by his own chat message at 12:06 (F9), and system records win over statements. This is the driver's own case against himself and NS-2 applies.

Endorsed: F1 shows a closest approach of 545 m and F2 shows the vehicle stationary 600 m away from 12:05:35 to the 12:09:05 cancellation (F3), so the entire stationary period was outside the pickup area required by NS-1(ii).
Endorsed: cumulative time inside 200 m was 0 seconds and the driver never entered that range after the alleged tap (F5, F1), so NS-1(ii) fails for the whole period and NS-2 mandates a full refund.

Endorsed, and it is the rider's strongest reliability point: the 12:06 message "I'm here already" (F9) was sent while the driver stood roughly 600 m away (F2), and the rider's contemporaneous reply "I'm at the pickup point and I don't see any car" (F10) is consistent with the GPS record.

Endorsed without qualification: $6.61 is on record (F3, F7) on an unconsummated RydeX booking with no surge (F8), and since the driver-initiated no-show fails NS-1 the fee is refundable in full under NS-2, payable as a voucher per NS-7.

Endorsed on the trigger: a recorded "I'm Here" tap (F5) while GPS shows the driver outside the pickup range (F1) is precisely the NS-2 account-review condition, and the rider's own clean record (F16) shows this is not a mirror complaint. The referral concerns the arrival-button signal, not whether the driver was a good wait-er.
Conceded as to the framework only: the $6.61 must be tested against NS-1's three limbs, and that is the test this brief has applied throughout (F3, F7).

C2 over-reads F6: the timeline is self-contradictory on the button press (F5 records a tap at 12:05:55 while F6 records null), so the rider cannot prove 'no press' — but nothing in NS-1 turns on the press alone, and even on F5's version the driver was 601 m from the pickup point with 0 s inside the 200 m radius (F5, F1).
Accepted: GPS puts the closest approach at 545 m with the driver never entering the 200 m range, so NS-1(ii) is not met and no advantage for the driver can be built on the arrival radius (F1, F2).
Accepted: the 3 min 30 s of standing time was served 600 m from the pickup point with 0 s in range, so the duration limb of NS-1 is satisfied in time but fails in place (F2, F5).

The driver's chat message "I'm here already" (F9) cannot survive the GPS record showing him 601 m out at that moment, so on this point the rider's reliance on system-over-statement is correct and my client's written statement (F12) is not evidence of arrival (F9, F5, F1, F12).

The full $6.61 refund follows from NS-2 once NS-1 fails on (ii) and (iii); the rider's clean 90-day record (F16) adds nothing to the finding, since the refund rests on the GPS record alone (F1, F2, F3, F7).

The button-misuse prong of NS-2 is not established because the timeline contradicts itself on whether any press occurred (F5 vs F6), and the driver is otherwise clean over 502 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes upheld (F17), so the refund stands but no account flag should be added.
